As we celebrate Women's History Month, we remember Hazel Raines. She the first woman in the state of Georgia to earn a pilot’s license. Raised here in Macon and a graduate of Wesleyan College, she earned both a private and commercial pilot’s license.

Raines became one of only twenty-five women chosen to fly with the British Air Transport Auxiliary (ATA) during World War II, flying damaged aircraft back to repair stations. During the war, she logged the most flight hours of any ATA pilot and survived a plane crash.

She continued her dedication and service to the U.S. military in 1950, when she was the first female reserve pilot called into active service for the Korean War.

She overcame asthma, a heart condition, and many other obstacles to achieve her goals. After her death at the young age of forty, Raines was dubbed “Georgia’s First Lady of Flight” and was inducted into the Georgia Women of Achievement in 1995.

Today, TSA personnel are missing their first full paychecks - thanks to Chuck Schumer and the caucus he leads. But what is ironic is that not one Senate Democrat who voted to deny paychecks for others has missed their own. 

I am so tired of politicians making a political point at the expense of the men and women who show up every single day to do their jobs and keep Americans safe. For a party that once resoundingly lectured against the dangers of a government shutdown, their current posture is as hypocritical as it is irresponsible. Senate Democrats have hijacked appropriations and shutdowns as their catchall for political leverage. 

But let me be clear: while that approach may serve their far-Left base and campaign strategy, it does nothing to safeguard the nation or support the personnel who carry out these missions everyday.

My statement on the House passage of my bill to end the Democrat shutdown and fully fund Homeland Security:

The Constitution places the safety and security of the American people at the center of the federal government’s responsibilities. It is a duty I don’t take lightly. Amidst rising global tensions and natural disaster possibilities, jeopardizing security operations and emergency preparedness is the last thing anyone should be doing. Yet, Democrats have kept the Department of Homeland Security shuttered for weeks – and again voted to keep it that way.

They are actively choosing to deny resources to the very people responsible for protecting the American homeland. Cybersecurity operations are at limited capacity, as adversaries like Iran, Russia, and China seek to exploit infrastructure vulnerabilities. Training for first responders has been canceled. FEMA grants – utilized by state and local entities to ensure safety and combat terrorism – can’t be accessed. TSA officers are being forced to work through the shutdown while missing paychecks. Coast Guard men and women, including those in harm’s way in Bahrain, are completing missions without full resources behind them. Even security preparations to keep attendees safe at the America 250 celebrations, the FIFA World Cup, the LA2028 Olympics, and more face disruptions. These impacts are not political or hyperbole. They are the direct cost of Democrats’ decision to play politics with the safeguards of this country.

My priority is serving and protecting Oklahomans and all Americans, which is why I voted again today to pass full-year DHS funding. No selective resourcing – full operational funding for the Department of Homeland Security and the personnel who stand watch over this nation every day. Despite bipartisan majorities in both chambers, a small minority of Democrats continue to hold this funding hostage. However, let me be clear: shielding the homeland should never be treated as a political bargaining chip.

RT by @chelliepingree: 🚨 FARM BILL POWER GRAB

The 2026 Farm Bill quietly slipped in three sections that could shield pesticide companies from lawsuits, block states from regulating chemicals, and weaken water protections nationwide.

Rep. Chellie Pingree just introduced an amendment to delete them entirely.

Here’s the plain-English breakdown everyone should understand 👇

1. Lawsuit Shield for Pesticide Companies (Section 10205)

If this stays in the bill, chemical companies could avoid liability even if new evidence shows their product causes cancer or neurological damage. As long as the pesticide followed the label approved under Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), victims may lose the ability to sue.

Why this matters:

Bayer has already paid about $11 billion to settle lawsuits over the herbicide Glyphosate linked to non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. More than 165,000 claims have been filed against Bayer tied to the product Roundup herbicide.

If Section 10205 passes, future cases like those could be blocked.

Pingree’s amendment removes that shield.

2. States Lose Power Over Pesticide Rules (Section 10206)

Right now states and local governments can create stricter pesticide protections than the federal government.

That includes things like bans on spraying near schools or buffer zones around homes and waterways.

Section 10206 would override those rules nationwide.

That reverses precedent set by the Supreme Court case
Wisconsin Public Intervenor v. Mortier, which affirmed that local governments can regulate pesticides.

Seven states currently allow local pesticide control.
Those protections could disappear overnight.

3. Weakened Water & Wildlife Protections (Section 10207)

This provision would exempt pesticides from additional review under major environmental laws including the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act.

In practice that means pesticides approved by EPA could enter rivers, streams, and habitats without additional permits or environmental review.

Government monitoring has already detected pesticide residues in most U.S. waterways, raising concerns about runoff impacts on fish, wildlife, and drinking water.

Why This Fight Is Exploding

Critics argue the provisions protect chemical manufacturers, override state authority, and weaken environmental oversight.

Supporters claim the sections reduce litigation risk, simplify national pesticide regulation, and protect agricultural production.

Pingree’s amendment simply removes the three sections entirely, restoring the existing regulatory framework.

What Happens Next

The bill is still in markup inside the House Agriculture Committee.

That means these provisions can still be removed before the Farm Bill moves forward.

This fight will determine who controls pesticide rules in America — communities or chemical companies.

Key Takeaways

The Farm Bill includes three provisions that could shield pesticide companies from lawsuits.

They could also strip states and towns of authority to regulate pesticide use locally.

Environmental protections tied to waterways and wildlife could be weakened.

The Pingree amendment would remove those provisions entirely and restore current law. @amtoxicology @chelliepingree

Nearly one-fifth of Americans are under 18, yet only 4% of federal cancer research funding is directed toward pediatric cancers, even though cancer remains the #1 disease-related cause of death for kids.

This is not simply an imbalance—it is a failure of priorities.

As Co-Chair of the Congressional Cancer Caucus, I’m working to change that through my Fairness to Kids with Cancer Act, directing research dollars toward the children who need them most and accelerating the search for cures.

من چندی پیش با رئیس جمهور اسلامی ایران، مسعود پزشکیان، صحبت کردم.
     
از او خواستم فوراً به حملات غیرقابل‌قبولی که ایران، چه به‌طور مستقیم و چه از طریق گروه‌های نیابتی، از جمله در لبنان و عراق، علیه کشورهای منطقه انجام می‌دهد، پایان دهد. به او یادآوری کردم که فرانسه در چارچوبی کاملاً دفاعی برای محافظت از منافع خود، شرکای منطقه‌ای‌اش و آزادی ناوبری مداخله می‌کند و هدف قرار دادن کشورما غیرقابل قبول است.

تشدید تنشِ مهارنشده‌ای که امروز شاهد آن هستیم، سراسر منطقه را به سوی هرج‌ومرجی سوق می‌دهد که پیامدهای سنگینی، هم امروز و هم در سال‌های آینده، به همراه خواهد داشت. مردم ایران، همانند همه مردم منطقه، قربانی این وضعیت هستند.

تنها یک چارچوب سیاسی و امنیتی جدید می‌تواند صلح و امنیت را برای همه تضمین کند. چنین چارچوبی باید تضمین کند که ایران هرگز به سلاح هسته‌ای دست نیابد و هم‌زمان به تهدیدهای ناشی از برنامه موشک‌های بالستیک و فعالیت‌های بی‌ثبات‌کننده منطقه‌ای و بین‌المللی آن نیز رسیدگی شود.

آزادی کشتیرانی در تنگه هرمز باید هرچه سریع‌تر برقرار شود.

همچنین از رئیس‌جمهور ایران خواستم که هرچه سریع‌تر امکان بازگشت سیسیل کوهلر و ژاک پاریس به فرانسه را ، در شرایط امن، فراهم کند. رنج آنان بیش از حد طولانی شده است و جای آنان در کنار عزیزانشان است.

I have just spoken with Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian.

I called on him to put an immediate end to the unacceptable attacks Iran is carrying out against countries in the region, whether directly or through proxies, including in Lebanon and Iraq. I reminded him that France is acting within a strictly defensive framework aimed at protecting its interests, its regional partners, and freedom of navigation, and that it is unacceptable for our country to be targeted.

The unchecked escalation we are witnessing is plunging the entire region into chaos, with major consequences today and for the years to come. The people of Iran, like those across the region, are paying the price.

Only a new political and security framework can ensure peace and security for all. Such a framework must guarantee that Iran never acquires nuclear weapons, while also addressing the threats posed by its ballistic missile programme and its destabilising activities regionally and internationally.

Freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz must be restored as soon as possible.

I also urged the Iranian President to allow Cécile Kohler and Jacques Paris to return safely to France as soon as possible. Their ordeal has gone on for far too long, and they belong with their loved ones.

Je viens de m’entretenir avec le Président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian. 
                    
Je l’ai appelé à mettre fin immédiatement aux attaques inacceptables que l’Iran mène contre les pays de la région, qu’elles soient directes ou via des proxies, comme au Liban et en Irak. Je lui ai rappelé que la France intervient dans un cadre strictement défensif de protection de ses intérêts, de ses partenaires régionaux et en faveur de la liberté de navigation, et qu’il est inadmissible que notre pays soit ciblé. 

L’escalade incontrôlée à laquelle nous assistons plonge toute la région dans un chaos aux conséquences majeures aujourd’hui et pour les années à venir. Les populations, en Iran comme partout dans la région, en sont les victimes. 

Seul un nouveau cadre politique et sécuritaire permettra d'assurer la paix et la sécurité pour tous. Un tel cadre doit garantir que l'Iran ne se dote jamais de l'arme nucléaire tout en traitant les menaces posées par son programme balistique ainsi que par ses activités de déstabilisation régionales et internationales.

La liberté de navigation dans le détroit d’Ormuz doit être rétablie au plus vite.

J’ai également exhorté le Président iranien à permettre au plus vite à Cécile Kohler et Jacques Paris de rentrer en France en sécurité. Leur calvaire n’a que trop duré et leur place est parmi les leurs.

Des médailles, du courage, une leçon de force pour tous : l’équipe de France a porté haut nos couleurs dans ces Jeux paralympiques.

Rendez-vous en 2030 dans les Alpes françaises pour ouvrir à nouveau grand les Jeux !
